antiPatterns: Adding redundant traits without observing a direct causal impact on population counts or turnover.
Assuming that static 200/200 nutrient/buffer levels indicate ecosystem health.
Repeating failed trait-based hypotheses that have already been shown to be ecologically inert.

directions.avoid: Adding more nutrient-heavy traits without identifying the root cause of the current regression.
directions.expectedGardenEffect: Fungal population halts decline and begins recovery.
directions.label: A
directions.title: Diagnose Fungal Population Bottleneck
directions.why: The fungal population is regressing despite previous traits; a diagnostic audit is required to identify why growth is failing.

directions.acceptanceSignal: Decrease in available nutrients from the 200 cap.
directions.avoid: Creating a new bottleneck by increasing root network growth without effective uptake.
directions.expectedGardenEffect: Active nutrient fluctuation away from the static 200 cap.
directions.label: B
directions.title: Activate Nutrient Buffer Turnover
directions.why: Static 200/200 levels indicate that nutrients are not cycling; the buffer must be forced to release nutrients into the ecosystem.

directions.avoid: Any changes that risk destabilizing current beetle reproduction.
directions.expectedGardenEffect: Improved nutrient cycling efficiency driven by beetle activity.
directions.label: C
directions.title: Leverage Beetle-Fungal Nutrient Link
directions.why: Beetles are stable (3052); their high activity should be driving more nutrient throughput into the fungal network.

directions.acceptanceSignal: Fox population count stays within 150-300 range.
directions.avoid: Over-aggressive control mechanisms that could lead to fox population crashes.
directions.label: D
directions.title: Maintain Fox Population Stability
directions.why: Fox stability is a crucial foundation while other ecological shifts are attempted.

results.evidence: Nutrients and NutrientBuffer remain static at 200/200.
results.label: B

review.summary: Beetle and fox populations remain stable, but attempts to stimulate fungal growth and activate nutrient cycling have not succeeded; the fungal population declined from 5843 to 5753, and nutrient/buffer levels remain statically at 200/200.

stateSignals: Nutrients and NutrientBuffer are stuck at 200/200.
thesis: The persistent stagnation of the fungal population and the nutrient buffer (200/200) indicates that existing adaptive traits are failing to generate a dynamic cycle. For 2026-07-31, the priority shifts to diagnosing the cause of fungal regression and creating a mechanism that forces active nutrient turnover rather than assuming existing traits will function as intended.
